findings.title: Controls are too close together
findings.explanation: 'Search' and 'Notifications' are 3 px apart and at least one is under 44 px: an easy mis-tap.
findings.recommendation: Keep at least 8 px between targets (more next to destructive actions), or merge rarely used actions into one overflow menu.

findings.title: Text is too small to read comfortably
findings.explanation: 10-px text is below the 12-px minimum for phones; secondary information (dates, tags, captions) becomes hard to read.
findings.recommendation: Use at least 12 px (13-14 px preferred) for secondary text and keep hierarchy with weight and colour rather than very small sizes.

findings.title: Touch target is too small
findings.explanation: 16×16 px: under the 44×44 pt Apple HIG minimum (24 px is the WCAG 2.2 floor); thumbs miss and hit neighbours.
findings.recommendation: Enlarge the hit area to 44×44 (padding, min-height/min-width, or an ::after hit-area) while keeping the visible glyph size.

findings.title: Bottom controls sit under the home indicator
findings.explanation: With the iPhone's 34-px bottom safe area emulated, this fixed control extends 34 px into the home-indicator zone, where swipes go to the system instead of the app.
findings.recommendation: Pad fixed bottom bars with env(safe-area-inset-bottom): padding-bottom: calc(8px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)).

findings.title: Focusing a field zooms the page on iPhone
findings.explanation: The field's font-size is 13 px; iOS Safari zooms in on any input under 16 px and leaves the page zoomed after typing.
findings.recommendation: Use font-size: 16px (1rem) for inputs, selects and textareas on mobile.

findings.title: Heading levels are visually inverted
findings.explanation: An h1 (17 px) is smaller than an h2 (19 px) on the same screen, so the visual hierarchy contradicts the document structure.
findings.recommendation: Make heading sizes follow their level, or change the element level to match its visual role.

findings.title: No pressed (active) state
findings.explanation: Pressing this control changes nothing visually until the action completes; on touch screens there is no hover, so this is the only immediate confirmation of a tap.
findings.recommendation: Add an :active style (darker tone, scale 0.97, or ripple) to every button and link variant.

findings.title: Page scrolls sideways (horizontal overflow)
findings.explanation: The page is 573 px wide in a 402 px viewport: content is cut off and the whole page wobbles sideways when scrolled with a thumb.
findings.recommendation: Let the offending element shrink (max-width: 100%, min-width: 0 on flex children) or scroll it inside its own container (overflow-x: auto).

findings.title: Uneven spacing between related elements
findings.explanation: Items of the same kind in one list or stack are separated by different gaps, which reads as grouping that isn't there and makes the list look broken.
findings.recommendation: Give the container one gap (flex/grid `gap`, or one margin rule for all items) instead of per-item margins.

findings.title: Keyboard focus is invisible
findings.explanation: Tabbing to this control changes nothing on screen (outline removed, no replacement), so keyboard users cannot see where they are (WCAG 2.4.7).
findings.recommendation: Never remove outlines without a replacement: use :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid <brand>; outline-offset: 2px }.

findings.title: Spacing does not follow a consistent scale
findings.explanation: Paddings, gaps and margins use many unrelated values, so the rhythm between elements looks accidental rather than designed.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a spacing scale (4/8-px steps: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32) as tokens and replace one-off values with the nearest step.

findings.title: Two primary actions compete
findings.explanation: 'Plan my day' and 'Add task' are both strongly filled, similar in size and side by side, so neither reads as the main action.
findings.recommendation: Keep one filled primary button per group; make the other secondary (outline or tonal).

findings.title: The same heading level has different sizes on different screens
findings.explanation: h2 is rendered at 19, 22 px depending on the screen.
findings.recommendation: Style headings once, globally, from the type scale.

findings.title: No hover state
findings.explanation: The pointer over this control changes nothing (colour, shadow, underline), so it does not signal that it is clickable.
findings.recommendation: Add a hover style (tone shift, underline, elevation) for every interactive component variant.

findings.title: Disabled control looks enabled
findings.explanation: This disabled control has exactly the same colours and opacity as enabled controls of its kind; users tap it and nothing happens.
findings.recommendation: Give disabled controls a distinct style (reduced contrast/opacity, no shadow) and cursor: not-allowed.

findings.title: Too many button variants
findings.explanation: 7 distinct button size/shape combinations (heights 28, 32, 40, 48, 52 px) at iphone17: buttons were styled one by one, not from a component.
findings.recommendation: Define 2-3 button sizes and 3 emphasis levels (primary, secondary, tertiary) as one component and use it everywhere.

findings.title: Controls stretch across the desktop window
findings.explanation: A 1366-px-wide input on a 1440-px screen: the mobile full-width style was never adapted, so the control looks bloated and the eye travels far.
findings.recommendation: Cap form and button widths on desktop (max-width 480-560 px) or lay forms out in a constrained column.

findings.title: Text is truncated
findings.explanation: Content is cut off with an ellipsis or clipped; on phones important words (task names, prices) disappear.
findings.recommendation: Allow two lines (line-clamp: 2) for primary labels, or give the label the space the trailing controls take.

findings.title: Unnecessary confirmation steps
findings.explanation: 'complete a task' asked for confirmation 2 time(s) for one action: friction that trains users to click through.
findings.recommendation: Confirm once at most — better, act immediately and offer Undo (a snackbar for 5-8 s).

findings.title: A tap produces no visible response
findings.explanation: In 'rename myself', tapping {'click': 'Save'} changed nothing on the page within 700 ms.
findings.recommendation: Acknowledge every tap immediately (pressed state, spinner, toast) even when the result takes time.

findings.title: Click target is below 24 px
findings.explanation: 16×16 px: under the WCAG 2.2 24×24 px minimum target size.
findings.recommendation: Enlarge the hit area to 44×44 (padding, min-height/min-width, or an ::after hit-area) while keeping the visible glyph size.

findings.title: Main action is at the top of the phone screen
findings.explanation: The primary action sits in the top fifth of a tall phone screen, the hardest zone to reach one-handed.
findings.recommendation: Repeat or move the main action to the lower half (a bottom action bar or floating button).

findings.title: A control is covered by another element
findings.explanation: Tapping the centre of this control hits a different element (often a fixed bar or floating button), so the control is hard or impossible to use.
findings.recommendation: Reserve space for fixed/floating elements (padding-bottom on the scroll area equal to their height) or move the floating element.

limits: Every viewport is browser emulation (Playwright + Chromium 153.0.8010.12); iPhone sizes are CSS pixels and safe-area insets are emulated through CDP (Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride). Safari-specific rendering (WebKit), the real on-screen keyboard and physical reach are not reproduced.
Browser chrome: the first screen is re-measured with the viewport shortened by 120 px (Safari's toolbars); dynamic toolbar collapse is not reproduced.
Keyboard interference: fields that would zoom on focus (font-size < 16 px) are measured; whether the on-screen keyboard covers a field is not testable in emulation.
Hover/pressed/focus states are sampled once per visual variant of control; focus visibility comes from real Tab presses (desktop).
Canvas-drawn interfaces (games): the DOM does not describe what is drawn, so DOM-geometry metrics cover only the HTML overlay (HUD, menus); use judgements for the canvas.
No physical-device evidence: findings are emulation results, not device results.
